name: Supervised Tutoring in Class
title: Supervised Tutoring in Class
answer: Supervised tutoring in class means students work with a school configured AI tutor while a teacher is present in the room and moving among them. The teacher's presence is what makes the tutoring work, because the teacher can see who is stuck, who is racing ahead, and who is using the tool to avoid thinking. It matters because the tool extends the teacher's reach during practice without taking over the teaching.

sections.body: This idea puts AI tutoring inside the classroom instead of leaving students to work with a tutor on their own. The teacher stays in the room and moves around, watching how each student engages with the tool. The problem it solves is that a tutor by itself cannot tell the difference between a student who is thinking hard and a student who is quietly avoiding the work, while a teacher can see those differences and respond to them. Setup matters as much as presence, because the tutor has to be configured to guide rather than to answer for the student. The tool is meant to extend what the teacher can do during practice, not to stand in for the teacher.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a classroom, the tutor is set up by the school, for example as a configured account in Gemini for Education, and students work with it while the teacher circulates. The tool should follow hint only instructions, asking the student what they have already tried and guiding one step at a time, and it should be given the correct answers and the common mistakes for that lesson. Students can work in pairs, which lets them talk through problems with each other as well as with the tool, and a pair may catch an error that a single student would accept. Talking with a partner also keeps the learning social, which the text says matters for motivation. The text does not describe separate versions of this practice for different grade bands.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text points to the Nigerian trial as the basis for this idea and cites De Simone et al., 2025. In that program, teachers received three days of training before the sessions began, and students worked in pairs. The text does not give a formal evidence label for this idea, and it offers no other study, figure or finding. What it states is that the teacher's presence is what made the Nigerian trial work.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets out clear limits. Supervised tutoring works best as part of a lesson, not as a replacement for one, and the teacher still does the teaching. A teacher might teach a concept, give a short period of tutored practice, and then bring the class back together to discuss what they learned. The tool must be configured with hint only instructions and supplied with the correct answers and common mistakes for the lesson, so that it guides rather than supplies answers. Judging who is stuck, who is racing ahead, and who is using the tool to avoid thinking stays with the teacher, and pairing students helps because a partner can catch a tutor's error that one student might accept.
